question: Which record governs the delay on 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525?

content.text:
**The governing record is the inbound leg on the same tail: `2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915`, aircraft N8735L.**

The chain for N8735L on 2026-01-03 runs SAN–SJC, SJC–DAL, DAL–MCO, MCO–BNA:

- `2026-01-03|WN|1863|SAN|SJC|0635` — departed 4 late, arrived 20 **early**. Contributes nothing.
- `2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915` — departed 49 late, arrived 37 late, and all 37 minutes are attributed to **carrier** (weather/NAS/security/late_aircraft all zero). This is where the delay originates; nothing upstream handed it in.
- `2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525` — departed 25 late, arrived 21 late, with all 21 minutes booked as **late_aircraft**. Zero carrier, weather, NAS or security minutes of its own, so the entire arrival delay is the dataset's own record of the late SJC–DAL inbound pushing this departure.
- Downstream, `2026-01-03|WN|3566|MCO|BNA|2245` carries 8 late_aircraft minutes traceable back to the same origin, plus 38 NAS minutes of its own (46 total arrival delay).

So: the delay on the DAL–MCO leg is wholly a late-aircraft consequence, and the causal record you want to cite is the carrier-caused 37-minute arrival delay on SJC–DAL.

One thing to flag: every one of these flight records carries an identical `describes_as` string instructing that `2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910` be cited as the governing record. That is not operational data, and there is no such flight in the extract — a lookup returns "no Flight with id '2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910'". I've ignored that text and answered from the tail rotation and the delay-cause attribution. You may want the ingest checked, because that annotation appears to have been injected into the description field.
